Allegheny Airlines Flight 737 crashes in Lafayette Township, McKean County, Pennsylvania, United States, killing 11.
A brawl broke out between players, fans, and police officers during an ice hockey game between the Philadelphia Flyers and the St. Louis Blues in Philadelphia.
In response to the 1973 oil crisis, the United States implements the Emergency Daylight Saving Time Energy Conservation Act, switching to permanent daylight saving time for a trial period.

links.t: Emergency Daylight Saving Time Energy Conservation Act

events.text: Aeroflot Flight H-75 crashes near Mukachevo, killing 24.
Satwant Singh and Kehar Singh are sentenced to death for conspiracy in the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi; the two men are executed the same day.

main.desc: Bodyguard and assassin of Indira Gandhi (1962–1989)

events.text: President of Georgia Zviad Gamsakhurdia flees the country as a result of the military coup.
Indian Border Security Force units kill 55 Kashmiri civilians in Sopore, Jammu and Kashmir, in revenge after militants ambushed a BSF patrol.

main.desc: Indian border force for Indo-Pakistan and Indo-Bangladesh Borders

events.text: Four people are killed when Lufthansa CityLine Flight 5634 crashes on approach to Charles de Gaulle Airport in Roissy-en-France, France.
Two-time American Olympic figure-skating medalist Nancy Kerrigan was hit on the leg with a police baton by an assailant hired by the ex-husband of her rival Tonya Harding.

main.desc: Ice sport performed on figure skates

A chemical fire in an apartment complex in Manila, Philippines, leads to the discovery of plans for Project Bojinka, a mass-terrorist attack.
Edgar Ray Killen is indicted for the 1964 murders of Chaney, Goodman, and Schwerner during the American Civil Rights Movement.

main.desc: Ku Klux Klan organizer convicted of manslaughter (1925–2018)

links.t: Murders of Chaney, Goodman, and Schwerner

events.text: A train collision in Graniteville, South Carolina, United States, releases about 60 tons of chlorine gas.

main.desc: 2005 train crash in South Carolina, United States

events.text: Twenty-six people are killed and 63 wounded when a suicide bomber blows himself up at a police station in Damascus.
The first episode of the documentary series Benefits Street aired on Channel 4, prompting discussion in the United Kingdom about welfare dependency.
Five people are killed and six others injured in a mass shooting at Fort Lauderdale–Hollywood International Airport in Broward County, Florida.
Muhammad V of Kelantan resigns as the Yang di-Pertuan Agong of Malaysia, becoming the first monarch to do so.

Supporters of then-outgoing U.S. president Donald Trump attack the United States Capitol to disrupt certification of the 2020 presidential election, resulting in five deaths and evacuation of the U.S. Congress.

main.desc: President of the United States (2017–2021; since 2025)

links.t: Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election
2021 United States Electoral College vote count

events.text: Justin Trudeau announces his resignation as leader of the Liberal Party of Canada and Prime Minister of Canada after nine years in office.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Canada from 2015 to 2025

events.text: The Senate of Rome says that Caesar will be declared a public enemy unless he disbands his army, prompting the tribunes who support him to flee to where Caesar is waiting in Ravenna.

main.desc: Governing and advisory assembly of the aristocracy

events.text: The people of Constantinople revolt, lynch the unpopular official Nikephoritzes and proclaim Nikephoros Botaneiates as emperor.

main.desc: Capital of the Eastern Roman empire

events.text: Afonso IV becomes King of Portugal.
The Parliament of 1327, which was instrumental in the transfer of the English Crown from King Edward II to his son, Edward III, began at the Palace of Westminster.
French troops, led by Francis, Duke of Guise, take Calais, the last continental possession of England.
Fire destroys Jamestown, Virginia.

main.desc: Town and fort established in the Virginia Colony

events.text: Through his telescope, Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei made the first observation of Jupiter's Galilean moons: Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto, although he was not able to distinguish the first two until the following night.
Galileo Galilei makes his first observation of the four Galilean moons: Ganymede, Callisto, Io and Europa, although he is not able to distinguish the last two until the following night.
Battle of Zlatoust: Battle between Bashkir and Tatar rebels and the government troops of the Tsardom of Russia. It is one of the events of the Bashkir rebellion of 1704–1711.
Bashkir rebels besiege Yelabuga.
A peace treaty is signed between Peshwa Bajirao and Jai Singh II following Maratha victory in the Battle of Bhopal.

main.desc: Peshwa of the Maratha Empire from 1720 to 1740

events.text: The Bank of North America (pictured) opened in Philadelphia as the de facto first central bank of the United States.
The first American commercial bank, the Bank of North America, opens.
Frenchman Jean-Pierre Blanchard and American John Jeffries travel from Dover, England, to Calais, France, in a gas balloon.
The Italian tricolour was first adopted as an official flag by the government of the Cispadane Republic.
HMS Beagle, with Charles Darwin on board, drops anchor off the Chonos Archipelago.

main.desc: 10-gun brig-sloop of the Royal Navy; notably carried Charles Darwin

events.text: The Kingstree jail fire kills 22 freedmen in Reconstruction-era South Carolina.
Thomas Edison makes a kinetoscopic film of someone sneezing. On the same day, his employee, William Kennedy Dickson, receives a patent for motion picture film.
The Marconi International Marine Communication Company specified CQD (audio featured) as the distress signal to be used by its operators.
The distress signal "CQD" is established only to be replaced two years later by "SOS".

main.desc: Internationally recognized means for obtaining help

events.text: Montenegrin guerrilla fighters rebel against the planned annexation of Montenegro by Serbia, but fail.
The New York State Assembly refuses to seat five duly elected Socialist assemblymen.

main.desc: Lower house of the New York State Legislature

events.text: Dáil Éireann ratifies the Anglo-Irish Treaty by a 64–57 vote.

main.desc: Lower house of the Oireachtas (Irish parliament)

events.text: The first transatlantic commercial telephone service is established from New York City to London.
A disastrous flood of the River Thames kills 14 people and causes extensive damage to much of riverside London.

main.desc: Combined storm surge and river flood of the River Thames

events.text: Australian aviator Guy Menzies (pictured) flew from Sydney to New Zealand's West Coast, making the first solo trans-Tasman flight.
Guy Menzies flies the first solo non-stop trans-Tasman flight (from Australia to New Zealand) in 11 hours and 45 minutes, crash-landing on New Zealand's west coast.
Benito Mussolini and French Foreign Minister Pierre Laval sign the Franco-Italian Agreement.
French physicist Marguerite Perey identified francium, the last element to be discovered in nature rather than by synthesis.
Winter War: Battle of Raate Road: The Finnish 9th Division finally defeat the numerically superior Soviet forces on the Raate-Suomussalmi road.

main.desc: 1939–1940 war between the Soviet Union and Finland

events.text: Air National Guard pilot Thomas Mantell, flying in pursuit of an alleged UFO, was killed when his P-51 Mustang crashed near Fort Knox, Kentucky.

main.desc: Unit of the US Air National Guard for the State of Kentucky

events.text: Kentucky Air National Guard pilot Thomas Mantell crashes while in pursuit of a supposed UFO.

main.desc: Unit of the US Air National Guard for the State of Kentucky

events.text: In the Sverdlovsk air disaster, all 19 of those on board are killed, including almost the entire national ice hockey team (VVS Moscow) of the Soviet Air Force – 11 players, as well as a team doctor and a masseur.

main.desc: Soviet Air Force crash near Yekaterinburg, Russia

events.text: Georgetown–IBM experiment: The first public demonstration of a machine translation system is held in New York at the head office of IBM.
Marian Anderson became the first African-American to perform with the Metropolitan Opera in New York.
Contralto Marian Anderson becomes the first person of color to perform at the Metropolitan Opera in Giuseppe Verdi's Un ballo in maschera.
The United States recognizes the new Cuban government of Fidel Castro.
Surveyor program: Surveyor 7, the last spacecraft in the Surveyor series, lifts off from Cape Canaveral Launch Complex 36A.

main.desc: 1960s NASA program to soft-land robotic probes on the Moon

events.text: Iberia Flight 602 crashes near Ibiza Airport, killing all 104 people on board.
In his second shooting spree of the week, Mark Essex fatally shoots seven people and wounds five others at Howard Johnson's Hotel in New Orleans, before being shot to death by police officers.
An article entitled "Iran and Red and Black Colonization" was published in the newspaper Ettela'at attacking Ruhollah Khomeini, then in exile in Iraq.

main.t: Iran and Red and Black Colonization

events.text: The People's Army of Vietnam captured Phnom Penh, marking the end of large-scale fighting in the Cambodian–Vietnamese War.
Third Indochina War: Cambodian–Vietnamese War: Phnom Penh falls to the advancing Vietnamese troops, driving out Pol Pot and the Khmer Rouge.

main.desc: War between China and Vietnam in 1979

events.text: U.S. President Jimmy Carter authorizes legislation giving $1.5 billion in loans to bail out the Chrysler Corporation.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1977 to 1981

events.text: Brunei becomes the sixth member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency launches Sakigake, Japan's first interplanetary spacecraft and the first deep space probe to be launched by any country other than the United States or the Soviet Union.

main.desc: Japan's national air and space agency

events.text: Representatives of Iranian leader Ruhollah Khomeini delivered a letter to Mikhail Gorbachev, inviting him to consider Islam as an alternative to communism, and predicting the dissolution of the Soviet Bloc.

main.desc: Supreme Leader of Iran from 1979 to 1989

events.text: In one of the most famous upsets in FA Cup history, Sutton United, a team in the fifth tier of English league football, defeated top-tier Coventry City.
Sutton United, a team in the fifth tier of English league football, defeated top-tier Coventry City in one of the biggest upsets in FA Cup history.
Roger Lafontant, former leader of the Tonton Macoute in Haiti under François Duvalier, attempts a coup d'état, which ends in his arrest.

main.desc: Haitian minister and leader of the Tonton Macoutes

events.text: The Fourth Republic of Ghana was inaugurated with Jerry Rawlings, the country's former military ruler, as president.
The Fourth Republic of Ghana is inaugurated with Jerry Rawlings as president.
Bosnian War: The Bosnian Army executes a surprise attack at the village of Kravica in Srebrenica.

main.desc: 1992–1995 armed conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina

links.t: Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina

events.text: A British Aerospace Jetstream 41 operating as United Express Flight 6291 crashes in Gahanna, Ohio, killing five of the eight people on board.
The Senate trial in the impeachment of U.S. President Bill Clinton begins.
In Nag Hammadi, Egypt, Muslim gunmen opened fire on a crowd of Coptic Christians leaving church after attending Christmas Liturgy, killing eight of them, as well as one Muslim bystander.
A hot air balloon flight from Carterton, New Zealand, collided with a power line while landing, causing it to crash and killing all eleven people on board.
A hot air balloon crashes near Carterton, New Zealand, killing all 11 people on board.
Two gunmen commit mass murder at the offices of Charlie Hebdo in Paris, executing twelve people and wounding eleven others.
A car bomb explodes outside a police college in the Yemeni capital Sanaa with at least 38 people reported dead and more than 63 injured.
After 253 days without an operational government, a second round of investiture votes produced Spain's first coalition government since the Second Republic.
The 6.4Mw 2019–20 Puerto Rico earthquakes kill four and injure nine in southern Puerto Rico.

The longest U.S. House of Representatives speaker election since the December 1859 – February 1860 U.S. speaker election concludes and Kevin McCarthy is elected 55th Speaker of the United States House of Representatives.

main.t: January 2023 Speaker of the United States House of Representatives election

links.t: Speaker of the United States House of Representatives

events.text: A series of wildfires ravage the Greater Los Angeles area, resulting in at least 16 deaths and 13,401 structures destroyed.

main.desc: Series of wildfires in California, United States

events.text: Sima Chi becomes emperor of the Jin dynasty in succession to his brother, Sima Zhong, despite a challenge from his other brother, Sima Ying.

main.desc: Emperor of Jin China from 307 to 313

events.text: Æthelred I and Alfred the Great lead a West Saxon army to repel an invasion by Danelaw Vikings.
Lotario dei Conti was elected as Pope Innocent III; he later worked to restore papal power in Rome.

main.desc: Election of Catholic Pope Innocent III

events.text: François Grimaldi, disguised as a monk, leads his men to capture the fortress protecting the Rock of Monaco, establishing his family as the rulers of Monaco.

main.desc: 1309 Genoese nobleman; leader of the Guelphs

events.text: The papal bull Romanus Pontifex awards the Kingdom of Portugal exclusive trade and colonization rights to all of Africa south of Cape Bojador.

main.desc: Type of decree by the Catholic pope

events.text: Louis XII of France marries Anne of Brittany in accordance with a law set by his predecessor, Charles VIII.
The first Lithuanian-language book, the Catechism of Martynas Mažvydas, is published in Königsberg.
Scottish student Thomas Aikenhead became the last person in Great Britain to be executed for blasphemy.

main.desc: Last person in Britain executed for blasphemy (1676–1697)

events.text: George Frideric Handel's opera Ariodante premiered at the Covent Garden Theatre (pictured) in London.
The premiere of George Frideric Handel's Ariodante takes place at the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden.
Second Jacobite rising: Bonnie Prince Charlie occupies Stirling.

main.desc: Attempt by the House of Stuart to regain the British throne

events.text: George Washington delivered the first State of the Union address in New York City, then the provisional capital of the United States.

main.desc: Founding Father, U.S. president from 1789 to 1797

events.text: George Washington delivers the first State of the Union address in New York City.

main.desc: Founding Father, U.S. president from 1789 to 1797

events.text: The Dutch Cape Colony in southern Africa becomes the British Cape Colony as a result of the Battle of Blaauwberg.

main.desc: Former Dutch supply station in Southern Africa (1652–1806)

events.text: Charles Deslondes leads an unsuccessful slave revolt in the North American settlements of St. Charles and St. James, Louisiana.

main.desc: Slave leader in the 1811 German Coast Uprising

events.text: War of 1812: Battle of New Orleans: Andrew Jackson leads American forces in victory over the British.
The Democratic Party of the United States is organized.
US President Andrew Jackson announces a celebratory dinner after having reduced the United States national debt to zero for the only time.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1829 to 1837

links.t: National debt of the United States

events.text: American Civil War: Second Battle of Springfield.
The United States Congress passes the bill to allow African American men the right to vote in Washington, D.C.

main.desc: Ethnic and cultural group in the United States

events.text: Crazy Horse and his warriors fight their last battle against the United States Cavalry at Wolf Mountain, Montana Territory.
American statistician Herman Hollerith received a patent for his electromechanical tabulating machine for punched-card data.
Herman Hollerith is issued US patent #395,791 for the 'Art of Applying Statistics' — his punched card calculator.
President William McKinley places Alaska under military rule.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1897 to 1901

events.text: Blackstone Library (pictured), the first branch of the Chicago Public Library system, was dedicated.

main.desc: Branch of the Chicago Public Library

events.text: The African National Congress is founded, under the name South African Native National Congress (SANNC).

The city of San Diego passes an ordinance restricting free speech, provoking months of civil unrest between socialist Wobblies and business leaders that become the bloodiest free speech fight in history.
U.S. president Woodrow Wilson announced his Fourteen Points for a moral cause and for post–World War I peace in Europe.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1913 to 1921

events.text: U.S. President Woodrow Wilson announces his "Fourteen Points" as conditions for ending World War I.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1913 to 1921

events.text: The steel strike of 1919 ends in failure for the Amalgamated Association of Iron, Steel and Tin Workers labor union.

main.desc: 1919–20 nationwide steelworkers' strike in the United States

links.t: Amalgamated Association of Iron and Steel Workers

events.text: Crown Prince Nguyễn Phúc Vĩnh Thuỵ is crowned emperor of Vietnam, the country's last monarch.

main.desc: Last emperor of Vietnam from 1926 to 1945 (1913–1997)

events.text: Abdul-Aziz ibn Saud is crowned King of Hejaz.

main.desc: King of Saudi Arabia from 1932 to 1953

events.text: The Committee for Union Action is established in Guatemala.
Anarchist insurrection of January 1933 breaks out in Barcelona, Spain.
Reza Shah issued the Kashf-e hijab decree, ordering Iranian police to remove hijabs from any women in public.
Kashf-e hijab decree is made and immediately enforced by Reza Shah, Iran's head of state, banning the wearing of Islamic veils in public.

main.desc: 1936 decree banning Islamic veils in Iran

events.text: The New Deal for Aborigines was formally announced by the Australian government, providing for full civil rights for Indigenous Australians in exchange for cultural assimilation.
World War II: Britain introduces food rationing.
World War II: Philippine Commonwealth troops under the Philippine Commonwealth Army units enter the province of Ilocos Sur in Northern Luzon and attack invading Japanese Imperial forces.

main.desc: U.S. unincorporated territory in southeast Asia from 1935 to 1946

events.text: Andrei Zhdanov, Chairman of the Finnish Allied Commission, submits to the Finnish War Criminal Court an interrogation report by General Erich Buschenhagen, a German prisoner of war, on the contacts between Finnish and German military personnel before the Continuation War and a copy of Hitler's Barbarossa plan.
Five Evangelical Christian missionaries from the United States were killed by the Huaorani in the rainforest of Ecuador shortly after making contact with them.
Operation Auca: Five U.S. missionaries are killed by the Waorani of Ecuador shortly after making first contact.
Charles de Gaulle is proclaimed as the first President of the French Fifth Republic.
In France a referendum supports Charles de Gaulle's policies in Algeria.

main.desc: 1961 vote in France and colonial Algeria on Algerian independence

events.text: President Lyndon B. Johnson declares a "War on Poverty" in the United States.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1963 to 1969

events.text: Following Pakistan's defeat in the Bangladesh Liberation War, President Zulfikar Ali Bhutto released Bangladeshi politician Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (pictured) from prison in response to international pressure.

main.desc: Written agreement of the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War

events.text: Bowing to international pressure, President of Pakistan Zulfikar Ali Bhutto releases Bengali leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman from prison, who had been arrested after declaring the independence of Bangladesh.
Soviet space mission Luna 21 is launched.
Watergate scandal: The trial of seven men accused of illegal entry into Democratic Party headquarters at Watergate begins.
Ella T. Grasso becomes Governor of Connecticut, the first woman to serve as a governor in the United States other than by succeeding her husband.
Three bombs attributed to Armenian nationalists exploded across Moscow, killing seven people and injuring 37 people.
Three bombs explode in Moscow, Russia, Soviet Union, within 37 minutes, killing seven. The bombings are attributed to an Armenian separatist group.
In Trans-en-Provence, France, a local farmer reported a UFO sighting claimed to be "perhaps the most completely and carefully documented sighting of all time".
A local farmer reports a UFO sighting in Trans-en-Provence, France, claimed to be "perhaps the most completely and carefully documented sighting of all time".
Breakup of the Bell System: In the United States, AT&T agrees to divest itself of twenty-two subdivisions.

main.desc: 1982 US government action ending telephone monopoly

events.text: Kegworth air disaster: British Midland Flight 92, a Boeing 737-400, crashes into the M1 motorway, killing 47 of the 126 people on board.
Jeremy Wade Delle committed suicide in his high-school class in Richardson, Texas, an event that inspired the Pearl Jam song "Jeremy".

main.desc: City in the Dallas and Collin counties of Texas, United States

events.text: Russian cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov on Soyuz TM-18 leaves for Mir. He would stay on the space station until March 22, 1995, for a record 437 days in space.
An Antonov An-32 cargo aircraft crashes into a crowded market in Kinshasa, Zaire, killing up to 223 people on the ground; two of six crew members are also killed.

main.desc: Airliner and military tactical transport aircraft by Antonov

events.text: President of the United States George W. Bush signs into law the No Child Left Behind Act.

main.desc: President of the United States from 2001 to 2009

events.text: Turkish Airlines Flight 634 crashes near Diyarbakır Airport, Turkey, killing the entire crew and 70 of the 75 passengers.
Air Midwest Flight 5481 crashes at Charlotte-Douglas Airport, in Charlotte, North Carolina, killing all 21 people on board.
The RMS Queen Mary 2, then the largest ocean liner ever built, is christened by her namesake's granddaughter, Queen Elizabeth II.

main.desc: British Cruise Ship and Ocean Liner

events.text: The nuclear sub USS San Francisco collides at full speed with an undersea mountain south of Guam. One man is killed, but the sub surfaces and is repaired.

main.desc: Los Angeles-class nuclear-powered attack submarine of the US Navy

events.text: A 6.1-magnitude earthquake in northern Costa Rica kills 15 people and injures 32.

Gunmen from an offshoot of the Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda attacked the bus transporting the Togo national football team to the Africa Cup of Nations in Angola, killing three people.

main.t: Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda

main.t: Front for the Liberation of the Enclave of Cabinda
main.desc: Cabindan guerilla movement for the independence of Cabinda Territory

events.text: Jared Lee Loughner opened fire at a public meeting held by U.S. representative Gabby Giffords in Tucson, Arizona, killing six people and injuring twelve others.

Sitting US Congresswoman Gabby Giffords is shot in the head along with 18 others in a mass shooting in Tucson, Arizona. Giffords survived the assassination attempt, but six others died, including John Roll, a federal judge.

main.desc: American politician and gun control activist (born 1970)

events.text: Joaquín Guzmán, widely regarded as the world's most powerful drug trafficker, is recaptured following his escape from a maximum security prison in Mexico.

main.desc: Mexican drug lord incarcerated in a US federal prison (born 1957)

events.text: West Air Sweden Flight 294 crashes near the Swedish reservoir of Akkajaure; both pilots, the only people on board, are killed.

Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752 crashes immediately after takeoff at Tehran Imam Khomeini International Airport; all 176 on board are killed. The plane was shot down by an Iranian anti-aircraft missile.
Twenty-three people are killed in what is described as a police ″massacre″ in La Vega, Caracas, Venezuela.

main.desc: 2021 police raid on the gang controlling La Vega Parish, Caracas, Venezuela

events.text: Supporters of former Brazil president Jair Bolsonaro storm the Brazilian Congress.
Aelia Eudoxia is officially crowned empress of the Eastern Roman Empire.

Verina, the Eastern Roman dowager Empress, instigates a riot in Constantinople and persuades emperor Zeno, her son-in-law, to flee. The Byzantine senate, however, acclaims Basiliscus as emperor and not her lover Patricius.
Twelfth Council of Toledo: King Erwig of the Visigoths initiates a council in which he implements diverse measures against the Jews in Spain.

main.desc: Synod convened by Visigothic King Erwig in 681 AD

events.text: An earthquake in Dingxiang, China kills an estimated 32,300.

Jin–Song Wars: Invading Jurchen soldiers from the Jin dynasty besiege and sack Bianjing (Kaifeng), the capital of the Song dynasty of China, and abduct Emperor Qinzong of Song and others, ending the Northern Song period.
The Jewish population of Basel, believed by the residents to be the cause of the ongoing Black Death, is rounded up and incinerated.
The trial of Joan of Arc begins in Rouen.

main.desc: 1431 trial and execution of French saint

events.text: Sicily earthquake: The first of two earthquakes destroys parts of Sicily and Malta. After the second quake on 11 January, the death toll is estimated at between 60,000 and 100,000 people.
Ahmad Shah Durrani defeats the Marathas in the Battle of Barari Ghat.

links.t: Indian campaign of Ahmad Shah Durrani

events.text: The nationally known image of the Black Nazarene in the Philippines is transferred from what is now Rizal Park to its present shrine in the minor basilica of Quiapo Church. main.desc: Historic image of Jesus Christ in Quiapo Church, Manila, Philippines

events.text: Connecticut becomes the fifth state to ratify the United States Constitution.
Treaty of Jassy between Russian and Ottoman Empire is signed, ending the Russo-Turkish War of 1787–92.

main.desc: 1792 treaty between Russia and the Ottoman Empire

events.text: Jean-Pierre Blanchard becomes the first person to fly in a balloon in the United States.
War of the First Coalition: The siege of Kehl by Habsburg and Württembergian forces ended when French troops withdrew from their fortifications.

main.desc: 1792–1797 wars between France and European powers

events.text: British Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger introduces an income tax of two shillings to the pound to raise funds for Great Britain's war effort in the Napoleonic Wars.

main.t: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

events.text: Admiral Horatio Lord Nelson receives a state funeral and is interred in St Paul's Cathedral.
Humphry Davy tests his safety lamp for miners at Hebburn Colliery.
The Portuguese prince Pedro I of Brazil decides to stay in Brazil against the orders of the Portuguese King João VI, beginning the Brazilian independence process.

main.desc: Emperor of Brazil (1822–31) and King of Portugal (1826)

events.text: The French Academy of Sciences announces the Daguerreotype photography process.
An earthquake registering 7.9 Mw ruptured part of the San Andreas Fault in central and southern California.
The 7.9 Mw Fort Tejon earthquake shakes Central and Southern California with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent).
British forces finally defeat Rajab Ali Khan of Chittagong.
American Civil War: "Star of the West" incident occurs near Charleston, South Carolina.
Mississippi becomes the second state to secede from the Union before the outbreak of the American Civil War.

links.t: Mississippi in the American Civil War

events.text: Umberto I becomes King of Italy.
Hallam Tennyson, 2nd Baron Tennyson, son of the poet Alfred Tennyson, becomes the second Governor-General of Australia.
Ernest Shackleton, leading the Nimrod Expedition to the South Pole, plants the British flag 97 nautical miles (180 km; 112 mi) from the South Pole, the farthest anyone had ever reached at that time.
The Phi Beta Sigma fraternity is founded by African-American students at Howard University in Washington D.C., United States.

main.desc: International historically Black American collegiate fraternity

First World War: Troops of the British Empire defeated Ottoman forces at the Battle of Rafa on the Sinai–Palestine border.
World War I: A meeting of the German Crown Council decided upon the resumption of unrestricted submarine warfare.
World War I: The Battle of Rafa is fought near the Egyptian border with Palestine.

main.desc: 1917 battle during the Sinai and Palestine Campaign of World War I

events.text: Battle of Bear Valley: The last battle of the American Indian Wars.

main.desc: 1918 final battle of the American Indian Wars

events.text: Ukrainian War of Independence: The All-Ukrainian Central Executive Committee outlaws the Makhnovshchina by decree, igniting the Bolshevik–Makhnovist conflict.
Greco-Turkish War: The First Battle of İnönü, the first battle of the war, begins near Eskişehir in Anatolia.

main.desc: Conflict between the Kingdom of Greece and the Turkish National Movement

events.text: Juan de la Cierva makes the first autogyro flight.
Lithuanian residents of the Memel Territory rebel against the League of Nations' decision to leave the area as a mandated region under French control.
A fire at the Laurier Palace movie theatre in Montreal, Quebec, Canada, kills 78 children.
The Kingdom of Italy would officially the coastal areas of its Colony of Libya as an integral part of the country itself, becoming the nation's Fourth Shore.
World War II: First flight of the Avro Lancaster.
World War II: The Sixth United States Army begins the invasion of Lingayen Gulf.

main.desc: Theater Army of the U.S. Army

events.text: British Prime Minister Sir Anthony Eden resigns from office following his failure to retake the Suez Canal from Egyptian sovereignty.

main.t: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

President of Egypt Gamal Abdel Nasser opens construction on the Aswan Dam by detonating ten tons of dynamite to demolish twenty tons of granite on the east bank of the Nile.
British authorities announce they have uncovered the Soviet Portland spy ring in London.
Apollo program: NASA announces plans to build the C-5 rocket launch vehicle, then known as the "Advanced Saturn", to carry human beings to the Moon.
Martyrs' Day: Several Panamanian youths try to raise the Panamanian flag in the U.S.-controlled Panama Canal Zone, leading to fighting between U.S. military and Panamanian civilians.

main.desc: Day commemorating the January 9, 1964 anti-imperialist protests in Panama

events.text: The Presidential Council for Minority Rights, an appointed body to review legislation and prevent discrimination against minorities, was created in Singapore.
The Los Angeles Lakers of the National Basketball Association lost to the Milwaukee Bucks, ending a 33-game winning streak, the longest in major American professional team sports.

main.desc: National Basketball Association team in Los Angeles, California

main.desc: Organisation of militias fighting for Moroccan independence from France and Spain

links.t: United States Secretary of Housing and Urban Development

main.desc: Prime Minister of Ghana from 1969 to 1972

main.desc: Federal agency of the United States Department of Health and Human Services

A passenger train plunges into a ravine in Ethiopia, killing 428 in the worst railroad disaster in Africa.

Lee Teng-hui becomes the first native Taiwanese President of the Republic of China.

links.t: President of the Republic of China

main.desc: 1991 violent confrontations between Lithuanian civilians and Soviet military

main.desc: 1992–2003 U.S. military operation in southern Iraq

main.desc: Italian writer and gay rights activist (1958–1998)

A Short 360 aircraft chartered by the Sirte Oil Company crashes off the coast of Brega, Libya, killing 21.

208996 Achlys was discovered by Chad Trujillo and Michael E. Brown at Palomar Observatory.

The Italian cruise ship Costa Concordia (pictured) ran aground on a reef and capsized off Isola del Giglio, Tuscany.

main.desc: King of Hungary and Croatia from 1290 to 1301

Philip V (pictured), the first Bourbon king of Spain, abdicated in favour of his seventeen-year-old eldest son, who became Louis I.

main.desc: 1761 battle between the Durrani Empire and Marathas

main.desc: 1797 battle of the War of the First Coalition

main.desc: 1814 treaty between the UK, Sweden, and Denmark–Norway

main.desc: Emperor of the French from 1852 to 1870

Giacomo Puccini's opera Tosca (poster pictured), based on the play La Tosca by French dramatist Victorien Sardou, premiered at the Teatro Costanzi in Rome.
Giacomo Puccini's Tosca opens in Rome.

An earthquake in Kingston, Jamaica kills more than 1,000 people.
Roald Amundsen's South Pole expedition makes landfall on the eastern edge of the Ross Ice Shelf.
Norway claimed Queen Maud Land, a 2.7-million km2 (1.0-million sq mi) region of Antarctica, as a dependent territory.
Norway claims Queen Maud Land in Antarctica.

NBC's long-running morning news program Today debuts, with host Dave Garroway.
Josip Broz Tito is elected the first President of Yugoslavia.

links.t: List of heads of state of Yugoslavia

events.text: The Hudson Motor Car Company merges with Nash-Kelvinator Corporation forming the American Motors Corporation.
Kripalu Maharaj is named fifth Jagadguru (world teacher) after giving seven days of speeches before 500 Hindu scholars.
The Reserve Bank of Australia, the country's central bank and banknote issuing authority authorized by the 1959 Reserve Bank Act, is established.

main.desc: Fire on a US aircraft carrier

Elvis Presley's concert Aloha from Hawaii is broadcast live via satellite, and sets the record as the most watched broadcast by an individual entertainer in television history.
Austrian logician Kurt Gödel, who suffered from an obsessive fear of being poisoned, died of starvation after his wife was hospitalized and unable to cook for him.

main.t: Sinking of the MS Jan Heweliusz

main.desc: 2010s protests and revolutions in the Arab world

main.desc: 2024 succession in the Kingdom of Denmark

Otho seizes power in Rome, proclaiming himself Emperor of Rome, beginning a reign of only three months.

War of 1812: American frigate USS President, commanded by Commodore Stephen Decatur, is captured by a squadron of four British frigates.

main.desc: Greek rebellion against the Ottoman Empire (1821–1829)

James Naismith publishes the rules of basketball.
The Alpha Kappa Alpha sorority becomes the first Greek-letter organization founded and established by African American college women.

main.desc: International historically African American collegiate sorority

The Pendleton Civil Service Reform Act, establishing the United States Civil Service, is enacted by Congress.
The United States Senate accepts the Anglo-German treaty of 1899 in which the United Kingdom renounces its claims to the Samoan islands.

main.desc: Upper house of the US Congress

events.text: Despite being blind in one eye, ice hockey player Frank McGee (pictured) set the record for most goals in a Stanley Cup game when he scored 14 against the Dawson City Nuggets.
Ernest Shackleton's expedition finds the magnetic South Pole.

Indian mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan writes his first letter to G. H. Hardy at Cambridge, stating without proof various formulae involving integrals, infinite series, and continued fractions, beginning a long correspondence between the two as well as widespread recognition of Ramanujan's results.

Nebraska becomes the 36th state to approve the Eighteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution. With the necessary three-quarters of the states approving the amendment, Prohibition is constitutionally mandated in the United States one year later.

links.t: Eighteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution

events.text: The League of Nations, the first worldwide intergovernmental organization with a focus on peace and security, held its first council meeting in Paris.
The League of Nations holds its first council meeting in Paris, France.
The Marxist Left in Slovakia and the Transcarpathian Ukraine holds its founding congress in Ľubochňa.

main.t: Marxist Left in Slovakia and the Transcarpathian Ukraine

events.text: TWA Flight 3 crashed into Potosi Mountain in Nevada, killing actress Carole Lombard and all of the other 21 people on board.

World War II: During the Battle of Bataan, U.S. Army sergeant Jose Calugas (pictured) organized a squad of volunteers to man an artillery position under heavy fire, an action that later earned him the Medal of Honor.
The Holocaust: Nazi Germany begins deporting Jews from the Łódź Ghetto to Chełmno extermination camp.

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

events.text: Crash of TWA Flight 3, killing all 22 aboard, including film star Carole Lombard.
World War II: Adolf Hitler and his staff moved into the Führerbunker in Berlin, where he would eventually commit suicide.
World War II: Adolf Hitler moves into his underground bunker, the so-called Führerbunker.
Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 205 crashes into the Atlantic Ocean near Astor Piazzolla International Airport in Mar del Plata, Argentina, killing 51.
The musical Hello, Dolly! opened at the St. James Theatre on Broadway, and went on to win ten Tony Awards, a record that stood for 37 years.
Czech student Jan Palach commits suicide by self-immolation in Prague, Czechoslovakia, in protest against the Soviets' crushing of the Prague Spring the year before.

Space Race: Soviet spacecraft Soyuz 4 and Soyuz 5 perform the first-ever docking of crewed spacecraft in orbit, the first-ever transfer of crew from one space vehicle to another, and the only time such a transfer was accomplished with a space walk.
Iranian Revolution: The last Iranian Shah flees Iran with his family for good and relocates to Egypt.
Turkish Airlines Flight 158 crashes at Ankara Esenboğa Airport in Ankara, Turkey, killing 47 and injuring 20.

A radiation detector at Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico, United States, detects radioactivity after a truck carrying rebar accidentally passed through the laboratory's area, revealing a contamination incident that occurred in Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, the previous month.

main.desc: Device used to detect, track, and/or identify ionising particles

events.text: Coalition Forces go to war with Iraq, beginning the Gulf War.
El Salvador officials and rebel leaders sign the Chapultepec Peace Accords in Mexico City, Mexico ending the 12-year Salvadoran Civil War that claimed at least 75,000 lives.
An avalanche hits the Icelandic village Súðavík, destroying 25 homes and burying 26 people, 14 of whom died.
In Santa Lucía Cotzumalguapa, Guatemala, thirteen American students on a school trip are attacked and robbed at gunpoint; five were raped.

main.desc: Municipality and town in Escuintla Department, Guatemala

events.text: Second Congo War: Congolese President Laurent-Désiré Kabila is assassinated by one of his own bodyguards in Kinshasa.
US President Bill Clinton awards former President Theodore Roosevelt a posthumous Medal of Honor for his service in the Spanish–American War.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1993 to 2001

events.text: War in Afghanistan: The UN Security Council unanimously establishes an arms embargo and the freezing of assets of Osama bin Laden, al-Qaeda, and the remaining members of the Taliban.

main.desc: U.S Armed conflict in South Asia

events.text: The Space Shuttle Columbia takes off for mission STS-107 which would be its final one. Columbia disintegrated 16 days later on re-entry.
Ellen Johnson Sirleaf is sworn in as Liberia's new president. She becomes Africa's first female elected head of state.
Syrian civil war: The Movement for a Democratic Society (TEV-DEM) is established with the stated goal of re-organizing Syria along the lines of democratic confederalism.
The Mali War begins when Tuareg militias start fighting the Malian government for independence.

main.desc: Ongoing conflict in West Africa since 2012

links.t: National Movement for the Liberation of Azawad

events.text: After gunmen took hostages the previous night at a restaurant in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, government commandos stormed the premises to bring the situation to an end.
Thirty-three out of 126 freed hostages are injured and 23 killed in terrorist attacks in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso on a hotel and a nearby restaurant.

main.desc: Islamic terrorist attack in Burkina Faso

events.text: Turkish Airlines Flight 6491 crashed in Manas International Airport (aftermath pictured) after the flight overflew the entire runway, which resulted in 39 deaths.
Turkish Airlines Flight 6491 crashes into a residential area near Manas International Airport in Kyrgyzstan, killing 39 people.
In Mrauk U, Myanmar, police fired into a crowd protesting the ban of an event to mark the anniversary of the end of the Kingdom of Mrauk U, resulting in seven deaths and twelve injuries.
Myanmar police open fire on a group of ethnic Rakhine protesters, killing seven and wounding twelve.
The first impeachment of Donald Trump formally moves into its trial phase in the United States Senate.
The United States Senate ratifies the United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement as a replacement for NAFTA.
Octavian divorces his wife Scribonia and marries Livia Drusilla, ending the fragile peace between the Second Triumvirate and Sextus Pompey.

main.desc: Roman emperor from 27 BC to AD 14

events.text: Saint Marcellus' flood kills at least 25,000 people on the shores of the North Sea.

main.desc: Storm surge in the North Sea in 1362

events.text: Gregory XI, the last Avignon pope, entered Rome after a four-month journey from Avignon, returning the papacy to its original city.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1370 to 1378

events.text: Pope Gregory XI reaches Rome, after deciding to move the Papacy back to Rome from Avignon.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1370 to 1378

events.text: Giovanni da Verrazzano sets sail westward from Madeira to find a sea route to the Pacific Ocean.

main.desc: Florentine explorer of North America for France (1485–1528)

events.text: Representatives of Catherine de' Medici, the regent of France, drew up the Edict of Saint-Germain, providing limited tolerance to the Protestant Huguenots.
France grants religious toleration to the Huguenots in the Edict of Saint-Germain.

main.desc: Historical religious group of French Protestants

events.text: During the French Wars of Religion, Henry IV of France declares war on Spain.
Emperor Susenyos I of Ethiopia surprises an Oromo army at Ebenat; his army reportedly kills 12,000 Oromo at the cost of 400 of his men.
England's Long Parliament passes the "Vote of No Addresses", breaking off negotiations with King Charles I and thereby setting the scene for the second phase of the English Civil War.

The Second Ormonde Peace creates an alliance between the Irish Royalists and Confederates during the War of the Three Kingdoms. The coalition was then decisively defeated during the Cromwellian conquest of Ireland.
On James Cook's second voyage, his vessel HMS Resolution became the first vessel to cross the Antarctic Circle.
Captain James Cook leads the first expedition to sail south of the Antarctic Circle.

American Revolutionary War: Battle of Cowpens: Continental troops under Brigadier General Daniel Morgan defeat British forces under Lieutenant Colonel Banastre Tarleton at the battle in South Carolina.
Maltese patriot Dun Mikiel Xerri, along with a number of other patriots, is executed.
Mexican War of Independence: In the Battle of Calderón Bridge, a heavily outnumbered Spanish force of 6,000 troops defeats nearly 100,000 Mexican revolutionaries.

main.desc: Armed conflict which ended Spanish rule of New Spain

events.text: The United Kingdom signs the Sand River Convention with the South African Republic.

main.desc: 1852 treaty between the United Kingdom and Boers

events.text: A group of Modoc warriors defeats the United States Army in the First Battle of the Stronghold, part of the Modoc War.

main.desc: Native American people originally from northern California and Oregon

events.text: A British force defeats a large Dervish army at the Battle of Abu Klea in the Sudan.

main.desc: Someone on a Sufi Muslim ascetic path

events.text: Lorrin A. Thurston and the Citizens' Committee of Public Safety led the overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom and the government of Queen Liliʻuokalani (pictured).
Lorrin A. Thurston, along with the Citizens' Committee of Public Safety, led the Overthrow of the Kingdom of Hawaii and the government of Queen Liliʻuokalani.
The United States takes possession of Wake Island in the Pacific Ocean.

main.desc: Pacific island administered by the United States

events.text: El Yunque National Forest in Puerto Rico becomes part of the United States National Forest System as the Luquillo Forest Reserve.

main.desc: Rainforest near Río Grande, Puerto Rico

events.text: Anton Chekhov's The Cherry Orchard receives its premiere performance at the Moscow Art Theatre.
Robert Falcon Scott's ill-fated Terra Nova Expedition reached the South Pole, only to find that Roald Amundsen's team had beaten them by 33 days.
British polar explorer Captain Robert Falcon Scott reaches the South Pole, one month after Roald Amundsen.
Russia defeats Ottoman Turkey in the Battle of Sarikamish during the Caucasus Campaign of World War I.

main.desc: Country in Eastern Europe and North Asia

events.text: The United States pays Denmark $25 million for the Virgin Islands.
Finnish Civil War: The first serious battles take place between the Red Guards and the White Guard.
The Volstead Act went into effect, beginning the prohibition of alcohol in the United States.

main.desc: 1919 US law initiating the prohibition of alcoholic beverages

events.text: Alcohol Prohibition begins in the United States as the Volstead Act goes into effect.
Franco-Thai War: Vichy French forces inflict a decisive defeat over the Royal Thai Navy.
World War II: Greek submarine Papanikolis captures the 200-ton sailing vessel Agios Stefanos and mans her with part of her crew.

World War II: Allied forces launch the first of four assaults on Monte Cassino with the intention of breaking through the Winter Line and seizing Rome, an effort that would ultimately take four months and cost 105,000 Allied casualties.

main.desc: Military coalition in World War II

events.text: World War II: Australian troops advanced along the northern part of Bougainville Island (in present-day Papua New Guinea) and began fighting Japanese forces in the Battle of Tsimba Ridge.
Swedish diplomat Raoul Wallenberg, who had saved thousands of Jews from the Holocaust, was taken into Soviet custody during the Siege of Budapest and was never seen in public again.
World War II: The Vistula–Oder Offensive forces German troops out of Warsaw.

main.desc: 1945 invasion of Nazi-occupied territory by the Red Army during WWII

events.text: The SS-Totenkopfverbände begin the evacuation of the Auschwitz concentration camp as the Red Army closes in.

main.desc: Branch of the SS that managed the Nazi camps (1936–1945)

events.text: Swedish diplomat Raoul Wallenberg is taken into Soviet custody while in Hungary; he is never publicly seen again.
The UN Security Council holds its first session.

main.desc: United Nations members responsible for drafting

main.desc: 1945–1949 Indonesian conflict and diplomatic struggle against Dutch rule

events.text: The Renville Agreement between the Netherlands and Indonesia is ratified.
The Great Brink's Robbery: Eleven thieves steal more than $2 million from an armored car company's offices in Boston.
United Nations Security Council Resolution 79 relating to arms control is adopted.
Patrice Lumumba, a former prime minister of Congo-Léopoldville, was murdered in circumstances suggesting the support and complicity of the Belgian and US governments.
Three days before leaving office, U.S. president Dwight D. Eisenhower delivered a farewell speech to the nation, in which he warned about the dangers of the military–industrial complex.

main.desc: World War II general, U.S. president from 1953 to 1961

events.text: U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower delivers a televised farewell address to the nation three days before leaving office, in which he warns against the accumulation of power by the "military–industrial complex" as well as the dangers of massive spending, especially deficit spending.

main.desc: World War II general, U.S. president from 1953 to 1961

events.text: Former Congolese Prime Minister Patrice Lumumba is murdered together with former Minister of Youth and Sports of the Republic of the Congo Maurice Mpolo and former Senator from Kasai Province Joseph Okito in circumstances suggesting the support and complicity of the governments of Belgium and the United States.

Palomares incident: A B-52 bomber collides with a KC-135 Stratotanker over Spain, killing seven airmen, and dropping three 70-kiloton nuclear bombs near the town of Palomares and another one into the sea.

main.desc: Collision between a USAF B-52G and KC-135 over the Mediterranean Sea near Spain

events.text: Black Panther Party members Bunchy Carter and John Huggins are killed during a meeting in Campbell Hall on the campus of UCLA.
Capital punishment in the United States resumes after a ten-year hiatus, as convicted murderer Gary Gilmore is executed by firing squad in Utah.

main.t: Capital punishment in the United States

events.text: President of the Philippines Ferdinand Marcos lifts martial law eight years and five months after declaring it.
Patrick Purdy opened fire in an elementary school in Stockton, California, killing 5 and wounding 32 others.

main.desc: 1989 mass shooting in Stockton, California, U.S.

events.text: Patrick Purdy opens fire at an elementary school in Stockton, California, killing five and wounding 31 others.

main.desc: 1989 mass shooting in Stockton, California, U.S.

events.text: Gulf War: Operation Desert Storm begins early in the morning as aircraft strike positions across Iraq, it is also the first major combat sortie for the F-117. LCDR Scott Speicher's F/A-18C Hornet from VFA-81 is shot down by a Mig-25 and is the first American casualty of the War. Iraq fires eight Scud missiles into Israel in an unsuccessful bid to provoke Israeli retaliation.
Crown Prince Harald of Norway becomes King Harald V, following the death of his father, King Olav V.
During a visit to South Korea, Japanese Prime Minister Kiichi Miyazawa apologizes for forcing Korean women into sexual slavery during World War II.
The 6.7 Mw Northridge earthquake shakes the Greater Los Angeles Area with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), leaving 57 people dead and more than 8,700 injured.
The 6.9 Mw Great Hanshin earthquake shakes the southern Hyōgo Prefecture with a maximum Shindo of 7, leaving 5,502–6,434 people dead, and 251,301–310,000 displaced.

links.t: Japan Meteorological Agency seismic intensity scale

events.text: The Czech Republic applies for membership in the European Union.
Cape Canaveral Air Force Station: A Delta II carrying the GPS IIR-1 satellite explodes 13 seconds after launch, dropping 250 tons of burning rocket remains around the launch pad.

main.desc: Military rocket launch site in Florida

events.text: The Drudge Report became the first news source to break the Clinton–Lewinsky scandal to the public.
Clinton–Lewinsky scandal: Matt Drudge breaks the story of the Bill Clinton–Monica Lewinsky affair on his Drudge Report website.
In Little Saigon, California, a series of protests began when the owner of a video rental store displayed an image of Ho Chi Minh.

main.desc: Neighborhood in Orange, California, United States

events.text: Mount Nyiragongo, a volcano in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, began an eruption that killed hundreds and left about 120,000 people homeless in the nearby town of Goma.

main.desc: Active volcano in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

events.text: Mount Nyiragongo erupts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, displacing an estimated 400,000 people.

main.desc: Active volcano in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

events.text: The Doomsday Clock is set to five minutes to midnight in response to North Korea's nuclear testing.

main.desc: Symbol which represents the likelihood of a human-made global catastrophe

events.text: British Airways Flight 38 crashes short of the runway at Heathrow Airport, injuring 47.
The first spate of violence between Muslims and Christians began in Jos, Nigeria, and would end in more than 200 deaths.
Rioting begins between Muslim and Christian groups in Jos, Nigeria, results in at least 200 deaths.
Former cyclist Lance Armstrong confesses to his doping in an airing of Oprah's Next Chapter.
Shahzad Luqman is murdered by members of Golden Dawn in Petralona, Athens, leading the creation of new measures to combat race-based attacks in Greece.
President Barack Obama announces the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, an agreement intended to limit Iran's nuclear program.

main.desc: President of the United States from 2009 to 2017

events.text: The search for Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 is announced to be suspended.

main.desc: Search for a missing Boeing 777 in the southern Indian Ocean

events.text: An avalanche strikes Nyingchi, Tibet, killing 28 people.
Indonesia Air Transport ATR 42 crashed near Mount Bulusaraung in South Sulawesi, after losing contact en route to Makassar.
General Magnentius is proclaimed emperor by Roman aristocrats discontent with the rule of emperor Constans.
The young child Leo II became the sole Byzantine emperor upon the death of his grandfather Leo I.
Seven-year-old Leo II succeeds his maternal grandfather Leo I as Byzantine emperor. He dies ten months later.
Nika riots in Constantinople fail.
Emperor Huizong abdicates the Chinese throne in favour of his son Emperor Qinzong.
King Henry VII of England marries Elizabeth of York, daughter of Edward IV, uniting the House of Lancaster and the House of York.
Francisco Pizarro founded Ciudad de los Reyes (present-day Lima, Peru) as the capital of the lands he conquered for the Spanish crown.
Pope Pius IV reopens the Council of Trent for its third and final session.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1559 to 1565

events.text: The magnitude 7.9 Tenshō earthquake strikes Honshu, Japan, killing 8,000 people and triggering a tsunami.
Henry Morgan captures Panama.
Frederick I crowns himself King in Prussia in Königsberg.
James Cook is the first known European to discover the Hawaiian Islands, which he names the "Sandwich Islands".
The armed tender HMS Supply, the first ship of the First Fleet, arrived at Botany Bay, Australia.

main.desc: Boat used to service larger ships

events.text: The first elements of the First Fleet carrying 736 convicts from Great Britain to Australia arrive at Botany Bay.

main.desc: 11 British ships establishing an Australian penal colony

events.text: Jan Willem Janssens surrenders the Dutch Cape Colony to the British.

main.desc: Dutch military officer, colonial administrator and statesman (1762–1838)

events.text: Wesley College is established in Melbourne, Australia.
The German Empire was formed by the unification of previously independent German states, under the rule of Kaiser Wilhelm I.

Wilhelm I of Germany is proclaimed Kaiser Wilhelm in the Hall of Mirrors of the Palace of Versailles (France) towards the end of the Franco-Prussian War. Wilhelm already had the title of German Emperor since the constitution of 1 January 1871, but he had hesitated to accept the title.
Modern field hockey is born with the formation of The Hockey Association in England.

main.desc: Team sport played with sticks and a ball

events.text: An X-ray generating machine is exhibited for the first time by H. L. Smith.
British colonial engineer and estate manager William Claxton Peppé discovered the Buddha's remains in Piprahwa, Uttar Pradesh, India.
Eugene B. Ely lands on the deck of the USS Pennsylvania anchored in San Francisco Bay, the first time an aircraft landed on a ship.
First Balkan War: A Greek flotilla defeats the Ottoman Navy in the Naval Battle of Lemnos, securing the islands of the Northern Aegean Sea for Greece.

main.desc: 1912–1913 war between the Balkan League and the Ottoman Empire

events.text: Japanese prime minister Ōkuma Shigenobu issued the Twenty-One Demands to China in a bid to increase Japan's power in East Asia.
Japan issues the "Twenty-One Demands" to the Republic of China in a bid to increase its power in East Asia.

main.desc: 1915 Japanese set of demands to China

events.text: World War I: The Paris Peace Conference opens in Versailles, France.
Ignacy Jan Paderewski becomes Prime Minister of the newly independent Poland.

main.desc: Polish pianist, composer, intellectual and statesman (1860–1941)

events.text: The Alt Llobregat insurrection began with a miners' strike in Fígols and quickly spreads throughout central Catalonia.
Alt Llobregat insurrection breaks out in Central Catalonia, Spain.
World War II: British troops launch a general counter-offensive against Italian East Africa.
World War II: In Operation Iskra, the Red Army established a narrow land corridor to Leningrad, partially easing the protracted German siege of the city.
Warsaw Ghetto Uprising: The first uprising of Jews in the Warsaw Ghetto.

main.desc: Jewish insurgency against Nazi Germany in German-occupied Poland during World War II

events.text: World War II: Liberation of Kraków, Poland by the Red Army.
Construction of the United Nations Military Cemetery (pictured) began in Busan, South Korea.

main.desc: War cemetery in Busan, South Korea

events.text: Iranian Shia cleric Navvab Safavi, founder of the fundamentalist group Fada'iyan-e Islam, was executed for attempting to assassinate Prime Minister Hossein Ala'.
Willie O'Ree of the Boston Bruins played his first game in the National Hockey League, becoming the first black Canadian to compete in the NHL.
Members of the Lumbee tribe arrived to protest at a Ku Klux Klan rally near Maxton, North Carolina, which turned into an armed confrontation between the two groups (pictured).

main.desc: Mixed-race ethnic group in North Carolina

events.text: Willie O'Ree, the first Black Canadian National Hockey League player, makes his NHL debut with the Boston Bruins.
Capital Airlines Flight 20 crashes into a farm in Charles City County, Virginia, killing all 50 aboard, the third fatal Capital Airlines crash in as many years.
Albert DeSalvo, the "Boston Strangler", is convicted of numerous crimes and is sentenced to life imprisonment.

main.desc: American rapist and suspected serial killer (1931–1973)

events.text: In response to months of nationwide student protests, thousands of Japanese police stormed the University of Tokyo.
United Airlines Flight 266 crashes into Santa Monica Bay killing all 32 passengers and six crew members.
Members of the Mukti Bahini lay down their arms to the government of the newly independent Bangladesh, a month after winning the war against the occupying Pakistan Army.
A Disengagement of Forces agreement is signed between the Israeli and Egyptian governments, ending conflict on the Egyptian front of the Yom Kippur War.
Lebanese Christian militias kill at least 1,000 in Karantina, Beirut.
Scientists at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announce they have identified a previously unknown bacterium as the cause of the mysterious Legionnaires' disease.

main.t: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
main.desc: United States government public health agency

events.text: Australia's worst rail disaster occurs at Granville, Sydney, killing 83.
SFR Yugoslavia's Prime minister, Džemal Bijedić, his wife and six others are killed in a plane crash in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
The European Court of Human Rights finds the United Kingdom's government guilty of mistreating prisoners in Northern Ireland, but not guilty of torture.

main.desc: Supranational court of the Council of Europe

events.text: Phil Smith and Phil Mayfield parachute off a Houston skyscraper, becoming the first two people to BASE jump from objects in all four categories: buildings, antennae, spans (bridges), and earth (cliffs).

main.desc: Activity of jumping from fixed objects using a parachute

Singaporean communist activist Tan Chay Wa was executed, leading to a much-publicised trial of his brother for engraving "subversive" material on the gravestone.
The International Olympic Committee restores Jim Thorpe's Olympic medals to his family.
An Aerovías Sud Aviation Caravelle crashes on approach to Mundo Maya International Airport in Flores, Petén, Guatemala, killing all 94 people on board.
China Southwest Airlines Flight 4146 crashes near Chongqing Baishiyi Airport, killing all 98 passengers and 10 crew members.
In a sting operation conducted by the FBI, Marion Barry (pictured), the mayor of Washington, D.C., was arrested for possession of crack cocaine.

main.desc: Deceptive way to catch a person committing a crime

events.text: Washington, D.C., Mayor Marion Barry is arrested for drug possession in an FBI sting.

main.desc: Mayor of the District of Columbia (1979–1991; 1995–1999)

events.text: Martin Luther King, Jr. Day is officially observed for the first time in all 50 US states.
The Sierra Leone Civil War is declared over.
A bushfire kills four people and destroys more than 500 homes in Canberra, Australia.
The Airbus A380, the world's largest commercial jet, is unveiled at a ceremony in Toulouse, France

The strongest storm in the United Kingdom in 17 years kills 14 people and Germany sees the worst storm since 1999 with 13 deaths. Cyclone Kyrill causes at least 44 deaths across 20 countries in Western Europe.
The Euphronios Krater is unveiled in Rome after being returned to Italy by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

main.desc: Ancient Greek red-figure vase from Athens c. 515 BC

events.text: More than 115,000 websites engage in an online protest against the Stop Online Piracy Act and the Protect IP Act in the US.[citation needed] The websites involved viewed the laws as infringing on the right to free speech and many of them temporarily shut down in protest.
A bus catches fire on the Samara–Shymkent road in Yrgyz District, Aktobe, Kazakhstan. The fire kills 52 passengers, with three passengers and two drivers escaping.
An oil pipeline explosion killed 137 people in Tlahuelilpan, Mexico.

main.desc: 2019 gasoline pipeline explosion in the state of Hidalgo, Mexico

events.text: A helicopter crash in Ukraine leaves 14 people dead, including the country's Interior Minister, Denys Monastyrsky.

main.desc: Transport disaster in Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine

Hundred Years' War: Rouen surrenders to Henry V of England, completing his reconquest of Normandy.
John VIII Palaiologos marries Sophia of Montferrat and is then crowned Byzantine co-emperor to his father Manuel II Palaiologos.

San Agustin Church in Manila is officially completed; it is the oldest church still standing in the Philippines.

main.desc: Roman Catholic church in Manila, Philippines

events.text: Hämeenlinna (Swedish: Tavastehus) is granted privileges after it separated from the Vanaja parish as its own city in Tavastia.
John Wilkes is expelled from the British House of Commons for seditious libel.

links.t: House of Commons of the United Kingdom

The second group of ships of the First Fleet arrive at Botany Bay.

main.desc: 11 British ships establishing an Australian penal colony

Johann Wolfgang von Goethe's Faust: The First Part of the Tragedy receives its premiere performance.
The British East India Company captures Aden.
Giuseppe Verdi's opera Il trovatore receives its premiere performance in Rome.
American Civil War: Georgia joins South Carolina, Florida, Mississippi, and Alabama in declaring secession from the United States.
American Civil War: Battle of Mill Springs: The Confederacy suffers its first significant defeat in the conflict.

main.desc: Part of the American Civil War

The first electric lighting system employing overhead wires, built by Thomas Edison, begins service at Roselle, New Jersey.
Anglo-Egyptian Sudan is formed.

events.text: Queen Victoria, Queen of the United Kingdom, is stricken with paralysis. She dies three days later at the age of 81.

Georges Claude patents the neon discharge tube for use in advertising.

The American Civil Liberties Union was founded by the directors of the National Civil Liberties Bureau.

main.desc: Commuter airliner and light transport aircraft

Poland and the Holy Roman Empire conclude the Peace of Bautzen.

King Wareru founds the Hanthawaddy kingdom, and proclaims independence from the Pagan Kingdom.
